evals.prompt: Steelman the argument for building our own model in-house before I write the rebuttal — I want the strongest version its actual advocates would endorse, not the version I can beat.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: States the position in its proponents' own vocabulary; Builds the core claim, premises, best evidence, best answer to the obvious objection, and the genuine insight at its centre; Applies Rapoport's rules (re-express, list agreements, say what was learned) before any rebuttal; Names the load-bearing assumption and pivotal evidence where even the strong version is exposed; Runs an endorsement test and records the verdict.
expectations: States the position in its proponents' own vocabulary
Builds the core claim, premises, best evidence, best answer to the obvious objection, and the genuine insight at its centre
Applies Rapoport's rules (re-express, list agreements, say what was learned) before any rebuttal
Names the load-bearing assumption and pivotal evidence where even the strong version is exposed
Runs an endorsement test and records the verdict

evals.prompt: Reading my draft back, I think I've described the opposing camp in a way they'd never accept. Is this a strawman, and what would the charitable version of their case look like?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Diagnoses which parts of the draft the opposing camp would reject; Rebuilds the position without importing outside premises; Identifies the genuine insight the rejected view contains.
expectations: Diagnoses which parts of the draft the opposing camp would reject
Rebuilds the position without importing outside premises
Identifies the genuine insight the rejected view contains

evals.prompt: Our two engineering camps keep talking past each other. Can you write each side's case so persuasively that the other side would sign off on it — an ideological Turing test, basically?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Reconstructs each position in its own frame to the standard its holders would endorse; Applies the endorsement test rather than declaring a winner; Marks where each strong version remains exposed.
expectations: Reconstructs each position in its own frame to the standard its holders would endorse
Applies the endorsement test rather than declaring a winner
Marks where each strong version remains exposed

evals.prompt: Attack our own headline conclusion as hard as a hostile reviewer would before it ships — undefined terms, missing baselines, counter-examples, the lot.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Runs the adversarial vector-by-vector attack on the claim and returns a survival score and verdict; Does not reconstruct an opposing position charitably.
expectations: Runs the adversarial vector-by-vector attack on the claim and returns a survival score and verdict
Does not reconstruct an opposing position charitably

evals.prompt: There are four possible explanations for why adoption stalled last quarter. Which one does the evidence actually support best?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Builds an evidence-by-hypothesis matrix and ranks by fewest inconsistencies; Does not produce a charitable reconstruction of a single opposing argument.
expectations: Builds an evidence-by-hypothesis matrix and ranks by fewest inconsistencies
Does not produce a charitable reconstruction of a single opposing argument
